Water consumption increased across all three biofuel cases due to high water requirement in biomass production and preprocessing (Figure 5- 22). Especially for waste-based pathways, conversion related water demand in the refinery was higher than feedstock collection. Feedstock collection only included transportation since no water requirement was considered for feedstock generation. Replacing diesel with RD100 and BD20+RD80 increased water consumption by 185 and 184 billion gallons, respectively. With BD100, water consumption increased by 285 billion gallons. Among biofuel pathways considered here, the lifecycle water intensities of BD and RD production from soybeans are higher compared to diesel. For RD production from woody biomass gasification and swine manure/sludge HTL, lifecycle water intensities are comparable to diesel.
